text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- European leaders meet in Amsterdam. The launch of a single European currency, the fight against unemployment and reform of the Maastricht treaty are on the agenda. At Friday's Franco-German summit in Poitiers, no agreement was reached on French demands for more emphasis on jobs, social issues in the stability pact. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation).
-- Socialists call for rise of more than four percent in the minimum wage. Public deficits may limit Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's scope to fulfill campaign pledges.
-- Minority shareholders call for Eurotunnel probe for alleged misuse of corporate funds and misleading information before 1994. Shareholders meeting scheduled for July 10.
-- Lagardere seeks ally in the telecommunications sector, considers strengthening ties with France Telecom notably on Internet services.
-- Airbus questions exclusive supply agreements between Boeing and Delta, American and Continental airlines.
-- French Finance Ministry to consider insurer GAN's restructuring plan, discuss it with the European Commission. Shareholders meeting may be postponed until after June 30.
-- Dassault Aviation chairman Serge Dassault calls for further restructuring of the French defence sector.
-- Daimler subsidiary Debis expected to announce whether it plans to increase stake in Cap Gemini or pull out.
-- European Commission considers changes in 1985 rules on asset management to protect investors.
-- Wine fair Vinexpo opens in Bordeaux, France.
-- Stakes are high as EU leaders gather for summit.
-- Irony in Franco-German debate - neither model works well.
